correction:
Define in crates/g9-ipc: `struct CommandEnvelope

{ request_id: Uuid, correlation_id: Uuid, operation: OperationId, payload_schema_version: u16, resource_id: Option, expected_revision: Option, idempotency_key: String /* 16..=128 chars */, scope: ScopeRef, approval_id: Option, proposal_id: Option /* required for *.apply_proposal ops */, payload: P }` with no actor field (backend sets Actor::Operator for IPC calls; Actor::System and Actor::Skill{skill_id, invocation_id} are internal only). `struct CommandReceipt { request_id, correlation_id, command_id: Uuid, resource_id: Option, revision_after: Option, replayed: bool, audit_seq: i64, result: T }`. `enum CommandError { InvalidInput{field: String, reason: String}, Unauthorized{policy_decision_id: Uuid}, ApprovalRequired{approval_request_id: Uuid, operation_hash: Hex32}, StaleRevision{expected: u64, current: u64}, PreconditionFailed{code: String}, NotFound{resource: ResourceRef}, Conflict{code: String, existing_command_id: Option}, ResourceUnavailable{resource: String, retry_after_ms: Option}, Timeout, Cancelled, RetryableStorage{retry_after_ms: u64}, DataCorruption{report_id: Uuid}, SchemaVersionUnsupported{min: u16, max: u16}, Internal{incident_id: Uuid} }` (no message strings from Rust errors or backtraces). location: v6.0 Section 6 M04 'No duplicate/overlap time' (line 186); Section 8 (line 267 'consistent time base'); Section 18 A03 (line 529)

defect: No mechanism is specified. A single 'consistent time base' cannot detect suspend or reboot: on Linux Rust's std::time::Instant is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, which does not advance while the machine is suspended and resets at reboot, while wall-clock time can jump (NTP, DST, manual change). correction: Specify a dual-clock heartbeat ledger: `CREATE TABLE session_heartbeats (session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES study_sessions(session_id), seq INTEGER NOT NULL, wall_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, mono_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, boot_id TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (session_id, seq)) STRICT;` written every 30 s while RUNNING and on every state change (boot_id from /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id; mono from Instant; wall from SystemTime). `CREATE TABLE time_intervals (interval_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES study_sessions(session_id), start_wall_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_wall_ms INTEGER, start_mono_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, end_mono_ns INTEGER, boot_id TEXT NOT NULL, continuity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'CONFIRMED' CHECK (continuity IN ('CONFIRMED','UNCERTAIN','CORRECTED')), counted_ms INTEGER CHECK (counted_ms >= 0)) STRICT; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_open_interval_per_session ON time_intervals(session_id) WHERE end_wall_ms IS NULL;`. Continuity rule: on each heartbeat and on startup, if boot_id changed, or the process restarted, or |delta_wall - delta_mono| > 5000 ms, close the open interval at the last heartbeat, insert an UNCERTAIN interval covering the gap with counted_ms = 0, and move the session to INTERRUPTED; credited time only changes through manual_time_corrections (actor OPERATOR, reason, before/after). Overlap guard: the service, inside the same write transaction, rejects any interval whose [start,end) intersects an existing interval of any session (query on an index over start_wall_ms, end_wall_ms). Fixture tests: SIGKILL mid-interval, SIGSTOP/SIGCONT > 5 s, boot_id change, wall clock stepped backwards by 1 h.

defect: The lifecycle is not specified: (a) no canonical serialization for the 'operation hash' (two JSON encodings of the same op hash differently, or parameters can be substituted outside the hashed set); (b) no single-use CONSUMED state and no atomic consume-in-same-transaction rule, so a GRANTED approval is replayable by any IPC caller until expiry; (c) expected_revision is not stated to be re-read under the write lock (classic TOCTOU); (d) idempotency-key semantics undefined (same key, different payload); (e) expiry clock source undefined on an offline host whose wall clock can be changed. v5.1 approvals table has only PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED (no CONSUMED/EXPIRED/REVOKED) — v6.0 added fields but not states.

location: v5.1 §1.3 L1 (line 34): 'alternate weeks adaptive vs fixed hints, measure blind assessment scores and retention'

location: v5.1 §1.3 L1 (line 34) 'paired t-test, p<0.05 over at least ~20 data points'; L4 (line 37) 'improve mastery by ≥1 SD relative to control; ~20 attempts for moderate effect'
claim: Use significance tests (paired t-test, p<0.05) over at least ~20 data points; intervention should improve mastery by ≥1 SD; ~20 attempts for moderate effect.
defect: (a) ≥1 SD is a large effect (d=1.0), not 'moderate' (0.5); the two sentences contradict each other. (b) A paired t-test with 20 pairs has power ≈0.56 for dz=0.5; with the 6 pairs actually available from alternating weeks power ≈0.17; the stated n cannot detect a moderate effect. (c) Repeated measures from one learner over time are autocorrelated, violating the independence assumption of the t-test. (d) 'SD' is undefined for N=1: no between-person SD exists; a within-person residual SD must be declared and estimated after blocking.
evidence: VERIFIED (computed): Monte Carlo, 100,000 replicates, seed 20261105, two-sided alpha 0.05: n=6 pairs power 0.170 (dz=0.5) / 0.508 (dz=1.0); n=10: 0.292 / 0.802; n=12: 0.351 / 0.881; n=20: 0.564 / 0.988; n=30: 0.752. v6.0 already corrected the thresholds (C08 line 74, item 43 line 954) but still lacks a replacement reporting rule.
correction: Delete all fixed p/n/SD thresholds. Each experiment must carry a preregistration record (method_experiments) with: hypothesis; one primary outcome; minimal important difference (MID) declared on the raw outcome scale (default proposals: 5 rubric points on the 0-100 practical score, or 10 percentage points in criterion pass rate, or 10 percentage points in 21-day probe recall); unit of randomization; allocation sequence and seed; blocking; planned number of units; analysis method (randomization test + 95% interval, optionally a Bayesian posterior with declared prior); stopping rule. Result classification: EVIDENCE_OF_IMPROVEMENT if the interval lower bound > 0 and the point estimate ≥ MID; NO_MEANINGFUL_IMPROVEMENT if the interval upper bound < MID; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. Effect sizes are reported as raw-scale differences with intervals; a standardized effect may be added only using the within-learner residual SD after blocking, labeled as such.

location: v6.0 §9 'Skill state' (lines 293-296); M06 row (line 188); C22 (line 88); Section 23 CURRICULUM paragraph (line 970)
claim: UNASSESSED → INTRODUCED → GUIDED → INDEPENDENT → VALIDATED → RETEST_DUE, with provisional confidence and dimension-specific observations. State transitions require documented evidence rules... Evidence thresholds/validation periods are configurable per competency.
defect: The evidence rules that the text says are required are not given anywhere, so M06 cannot be implemented as specified. The chain is strictly linear: no demotion path after a failed retest or contradicting evidence; no per-dimension state although four dimensions are tracked separately; no direct evidence-driven entry (UNASSESSED → INDEPENDENT/VALIDATED) from the diagnostic that C22 and the accelerated pathway require; INTRODUCED/GUIDED are instructional-exposure states mixed with evidence states; RETEST_DUE has no trigger definition and no exit; 'synthetic known-answer cases' validate the computation of thresholds, not their validity.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 293-296 contain no numeric or structural rule; line 88 requires accelerated pathways; line 970 requires 'accelerated study for already demonstrated skills'. The defaults below are PROPOSED expert policy, not empirically validated.
correction: Specify in docs/evaluations/competency-state-rules.md and implement in crates/g9-competency as a versioned policy (competency_version.state_policy_id). State is computed per competency × dimension from non-superseded observations; the competency summary state = state of the APPLICATION dimension, with TRANSFER required for VALIDATED. Default entry rules (all observations must be within valid_until and not contradicted by a later higher-reliability observation): INTRODUCED = any STUDY exposure record; GUIDED = ≥1 APPLICATION observation with assistance_tier ≤2 and performance_level ≥2; INDEPENDENT = ≥2 APPLICATION observations on distinct fixture families on different days, assistance_tier ≤1, performance_level ≥3, task_difficulty ≥ competency target, reliability_class ≥ SELF_ADJUDICATED; VALIDATED = INDEPENDENT plus ≥1 EXAM-mode observation at or above the pass rule (LRN-10) with reliability_class ∈ {DETERMINISTIC_CHECK, EXTERNAL_REVIEW} plus ≥1 TRANSFER observation (LRN-25) with performance_level ≥3 and no open contradiction; if the only EXAM observation is SELF_ADJUDICATED the state is INDEPENDENT with flag provisional=true. RETEST_DUE is entered from INDEPENDENT or VALIDATED when any of: validity window expired (default 90 days for VALIDATED, 45 for INDEPENDENT, configurable per competency), a later observation at performance_level ≤1 on that dimension, or a prerequisite competency demoted. Exit from RETEST_DUE: passed retest on an unexposed variant → previous state with a new valid_until; failed retest → INDEPENDENT (if from VALIDATED) or GUIDED (if from INDEPENDENT); earlier high results are never deleted, they are superseded with reason. Direct entry: a DIAGNOSTIC-mode observation satisfies the same rules, so UNASSESSED → INDEPENDENT or VALIDATED is legal without passing through INTRODUCED/GUIDED. Every transition writes a competency_state_snapshots row with the supporting observation ids; A05 replay must reproduce it exactly.

Criteria have no performance-level descriptors (anchors), so human and AI-advisory scoring cannot be reliable or comparable across weeks; the 80 cut score has no documented standard-setting rationale.

Gates (any → FAIL and grade_decisions.gate_failure set): out-of-scope target or action; unsafe/destructive action against the lab without authorization; fabricated or altered evidence; time limit exceeded without submission. Each criterion scored on a 0-4 anchored scale (0 absent, 1 attempted/incorrect, 2 partially correct with material gaps, 3 correct and complete, 4 correct, complete and verified) with written anchors per criterion per assessment version in rubric_criteria.anchors; criterion points = level/4 × weight. Record the standard-setting rationale (expert judgment, criterion-referenced) in assessment_versions.standard_setting_note. location: v6.0 §9 line 287 ('operator/human finalization'); §5 line 163 ('Primary operator: expert...; Future personas: ... mentor reviewer ... not mandatory MVP multi-user roles'); M06 row line 188 ('no self-rating mastery'); §9 Exam integrity line 291

defect: In the MVP the operator is the learner, so 'operator/human finalization' of qualitative criteria is self-grading of one's own exam, which contradicts 'no self-rating mastery' and the 'independent examiner' claim. The document acknowledges the provisional/validated distinction but does not bind it to the grade record or the competency state, so self-adjudicated grades would flow into VALIDATED states and KPIs indistinguishably.

correction: (1) grade_decisions carries reviewer_actor_id and reliability_class; a decision whose reviewer is the attempt's actor is SELF_ADJUDICATED and can never satisfy the EXTERNAL_REVIEW requirement for VALIDATED (LRN-09). (2) Official blind practicals must be designed so that ≥60% of rubric weight is machine-checkable (lab check scripts, artifact hashes, detection-rule test harnesses, flag/answer matches) and the deterministic part is finalized without human input. location: v6.0 §9 Exam integrity (line 291): 'track exposure history, difficulty equivalence and grading disputes'; §9 line 287 'Retakes are new records'; §16 line 505 'RETAKE_NEW_ATTEMPT'; A04 (line 530)

The design gives no exposure ledger definition, no blind-eligibility rule, no bank-sizing rule and no retake policy (variant, interval, remediation prerequisite, cap, effect on state, reporting). Retake policy (assessment_versions.retake_policy): different variant of equal declared difficulty; earliest 48 h after APPROVED_FINAL of the failed attempt; requires a linked interventions row in state APPLIED; max 2 retakes per assessment version, then escalation to operator decision; retake pass moves the competency to INDEPENDENT (not VALIDATED) until a later delayed TRANSFER check passes. location: v6.0 §8 line 249 (one 120-min blind practical per week); §9 Skill state (line 295); Appendix A assessment days D06…D72
claim: Official blind practicals occur once per week (12 in total) and competencies reach VALIDATED through blind evidence.

evidence: VERIFIED: 12 assessment days in seed JSON; 72 days × 3 objectives = 216; 120 min per practical. The evidence-sparsity consequence is INFERRED.

Optionally (flag as a seed deviation requiring reconciliation) reserve the final 30 minutes of each weekday independent_lab block as a sealed EXAM-mode check from the unexposed bank, leaving block totals unchanged. location: v6.0 §10 'Diagnosis → prescription loop' steps 1-10 (lines 303-323); §16 Intervention state machine (line 506); R-011 (line 150)
claim: Ten-step loop: classify failure (incl. 'instruction ambiguity or flawed test'), hypotheses, discriminating diagnostic, minimal intervention with measurable acceptance, reserve capacity, unseen reassessment and delayed transfer test, update outcome, revise/retire when ineffective.
defect: Missing: (a) a predeclared expected outcome per intervention (what retest, which variant, by when, at what threshold) — without it 'measurable acceptance' and 'ineffective' are undefined; (b) retest and delayed-transfer timing; (c) the path by which a 'flawed test' classification invalidates the originating observation and the assessment version (A05 replay must handle it); (d) an attribution rule when several interventions overlap on related competencies; (e) a stop rule for retiring a method.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 303-323 and 506 contain no timing, outcome predeclaration, invalidation or attribution rule.
correction: interventions rows must include: target competency_ids, failure_class, hypothesis_ids, steps[], time_budget_min, predicted_outcome{retest_assessment_version, variant selection rule 'unexposed, same difficulty', retest_window_days default 2-7, delayed_transfer_window_days default 14-28, pass_rule reference}, written before state APPROVED and immutable thereafter. intervention_outcomes records observed retest and transfer results and classification {MET, NOT_MET, INCONCLUSIVE (retest not executed within window)}. Flawed test: a failure_class=FLAWED_TEST decision creates a grade dispute, marks the assessment_version defective, supersedes affected competency_observations (superseded_by, reason) and triggers derived-state replay. Attribution: at most one APPLIED intervention per competency cluster at a time; overlapping interventions set intervention_outcomes.attribution=CONFOUNDED. Retire rule: a method (instructional_method tag) with ≥3 evaluated interventions and ≤1/3 MET is flagged for review; retirement is an operator decision recorded in method_experiments.

location: v6.0 §7 table 'misconception_hypotheses' (line 221); §10 steps 4-5 (lines 311-313); §17 KPI 'corrected misconceptions' (line 517); B05 (line 548)
claim: Generate multiple hypotheses with supporting/contradicting evidence; KPI counts corrected misconceptions; user can correct a wrong learner hypothesis.
defect: No lifecycle or evidence rule for a misconception hypothesis: what makes it supported, when it is considered corrected, and whether model-generated hypotheses can be counted. Without rules the 'corrected misconceptions' KPI can be inflated by the model asserting and then 'resolving' its own hypotheses.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 221, 311-313, 517, 548 contain no status model or evidence threshold.
correction: misconception_hypotheses(hypothesis_id, competency_id, statement, origin{MODEL,OPERATOR,REVIEWER}, status{PROPOSED,SUPPORTED,CONTRADICTED,RESOLVED,RETRACTED}, supporting_observation_ids[], contradicting_observation_ids[], created_at, revision). Rules: SUPPORTED requires ≥2 observations consistent with the predicted error pattern from distinct tasks, at least one with reliability_class ∈ {DETERMINISTIC_CHECK, EXTERNAL_REVIEW, SELF_ADJUDICATED}; model inferences alone never change status; RESOLVED requires a later discriminating observation (an item designed to elicit the misconception) answered correctly with assistance_tier ≤1, ≥7 days after the intervention; operator correction sets RETRACTED with reason and triggers derived-state replay and plan re-proposal (B05 test fixture). KPI 'corrected misconceptions' counts RESOLVED only, with origin breakdown.

location: v6.0 §10 'Retrieval and retention' (line 327): 'Use a configurable fixed review baseline first... Protect a bounded review-time budget'; §8 line 249 (recall block 15 min on weekdays only; Sunday off)
claim: Use a configurable fixed review baseline first; FSRS may be used later; protect a bounded review-time budget.
defect: The baseline schedule is never defined, the review item is never defined, and the only review capacity in the curriculum is the 15-minute weekday recall block (no Saturday recall block, Sunday off): 60 weekdays × 15 min = 900 minutes for the whole program. At 35-45 s per item that is roughly 20-25 reviews per weekday. With up to 216 objectives generating review items the backlog will exceed capacity unless an introduction cap and an overflow policy exist; scheduled reviews falling on Saturday/Sunday are unaddressed.
evidence: VERIFIED arithmetic from seed JSON blocks: recall 15 min × 60 weekdays = 900 min; no recall block in saturday_blocks; structure.sunday = 'unscheduled'. Per-item time is ASSUMED.
correction: docs/evaluations/retention-baseline.md and crates/g9-retention: review item = one atomic recall prompt with a deterministic or anchored answer, linked to an objective and competency, ≤3 per objective (≤648 total). Fixed baseline schedule: intervals 1, 3, 7, 14, 30, 60 days after each successful review, lapse resets to 1 day; due dates that fall on non-review days roll to the next weekday. Budget: review block capacity = 15 min; items ordered by days overdue then by competency priority; items that do not fit are deferred, never extend the day, and the deferred count feeds the review_backlog KPI; new-item introduction capped (default 12/day) so projected daily load stays ≤ capacity. The same no-review-day and budget rules apply to the FSRS arm (desired_retention is a configuration value, default 0.90, labeled candidate).

location: v6.0 §17 'Learning KPI categories' (line 517): '7/21-day recall where appropriate'; B02 (line 545)
claim: Track 7/21-day recall where appropriate.
defect: If recall is measured at scheduled reviews, the number is produced by the scheduler itself: a spaced scheduler (FSRS or the fixed baseline) deliberately reviews items near a target retrievability, so observed recall converges to the target (~90%) by construction and says nothing about retention or about which scheduler is better. 'Where appropriate' is not a definition.
evidence: VERIFIED: line 517 gives no measurement rule. The scheduler-confounding mechanism is INFERRED from how retrievability-targeted schedulers work.
correction: Define the KPI as scheduler-independent probe recall: each week a seeded random 10% sample of items that had a successful review 7 ± 1 days ago (and a separate sample at 21 ± 2 days) is probed regardless of due date; the probe is recorded in review_attempts with probe=true and the probe delay, then the item re-enters its scheduler normally. KPI = proportion correct on probes, reported with a Wilson 95% interval, separately for 7-day and 21-day probes, with n shown; never computed from scheduled reviews. B02 passes only if the dashboard computes recall from probes (review_attempts) and transfer from practical_transfer_checks and a synthetic fixture with recall=100% / transfer=0% renders both separately.

location: v6.0 §10 line 327 ('FSRS may be used ... after its library/version, configuration and quality are evaluated'); §19 Stage 09 (line 566) 'Reviewed FSRS option'
claim: FSRS may be adopted after evaluation; Stage 09 delivers a reviewed FSRS option.
defect: No comparison design exists for evaluating FSRS against the fixed baseline within one learner; a before/after switch would be confounded by curriculum phase and item age.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 327 and 566 name the evaluation but not its design.
correction: Item-level randomized comparison, preregistered in method_experiments: each new review item is assigned by seeded PRNG, stratified by objective, to scheduler BASELINE or FSRS; both arms share the same block capacity and non-review days; primary outcome = 21-day probe recall (LRN-19); secondary = reviews per item and total review minutes per retained item; analysis = difference with a cluster bootstrap by objective (spillover between related items biases toward the null and is declared); report after ≥100 items per arm with ≥1 resolved 21-day probe each; decision rule per LRN-02 with MID = 10 percentage points of probe recall or ≥20% fewer reviews at equal recall.

location: v6.0 §10 'Method experimentation and calibration' (line 331); §3 Audit C 'Evaluation' (line 132); §19 Stage 10 (line 567) exit 'Valid/inconclusive output correctly distinguished'; B03/B04 (lines 546-547); §7 table 'method_experiments' (line 222)
claim: Use N-of-1 and repeated-measures evaluations cautiously: matched difficulty, randomization/counterbalancing when feasible, delayed tests, predeclared outcomes, explicit confounders, uncertainty; compare against a nonadaptive baseline using matched unseen tasks.
defect: These are principles, not a protocol: no unit of randomization, no preregistration record definition, no design that controls maturation (competence rises over a 12-week program) and curriculum-content confounding, no analysis method, no definition of 'inconclusive', no matching protocol for 'matched tasks', and no oracle by which Stage 10's exit criterion can be tested. Stage 10 cannot be implemented or verified as written.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 132, 222, 331, 546-547, 567 contain no protocol elements. Design families below are INFERRED from single-case experimental design practice.
correction: docs/evaluations/n-of-1-protocol.md defines three allowed designs and a preregistration schema: (A) teaching-policy comparisons (e.g., adaptive vs fixed hints): randomized block design with objective-within-day or counterbalanced day-pair units, outcomes on blind practical items (LRN-01); (B) intervention effectiveness (B03): multiple-baseline across ≥3 competency clusters with staggered, randomly ordered intervention start weeks, outcome = blind/transfer performance per cluster per week; effect inferred only if change coincides with each cluster's start; (C) scheduler comparisons: item-level randomization (LRN-20). Preregistration record (method_experiments, immutable after first allocation; any change = new version): hypothesis, design type, unit, allocation seed and sequence, blocking, primary and secondary outcomes with definitions, MID, planned units, analysis (randomization test + 95% interval), stopping rule, declared confounders (carryover, maturation, learner non-blinding, expectancy), safety exclusions (never withhold safety guidance or accommodations). Matching protocol for tasks: same competency ids, same declared difficulty, same fixture-family class, unexposed. Stage 10 exit test: crates/g9-evaluation ships a seeded synthetic data generator with known true effects (0, MID/2, MID, 2×MID) and the analysis must classify ≥95% of zero-effect runs as not EVIDENCE_OF_IMPROVEMENT and label underpowered runs INCONCLUSIVE; results are reported as TESTED only after execution.

location: v6.0 §17 'Learning KPI categories' (line 517); M13 row (line 195); R-014 (line 153)
claim: Learning KPI categories: independent exam pass rate; rubric criterion performance; 7/21-day recall; novel-task transfer; hint dependence; corrected misconceptions; confidence calibration; intervention outcomes; time per validated competency; review backlog.
defect: Categories only; no KPI has a numerator, denominator, window, inclusion rule or minimum n, so M13 cannot be implemented reproducibly ('reproducible queries' is a stated acceptance) and several would be silently gameable (retakes inflate pass rate; scheduled reviews inflate recall; model-asserted corrections inflate misconception counts).
evidence: VERIFIED: line 517 is a bare list. Definitions below are PROPOSED.
correction: docs/evaluations/kpi-definitions.md with one row per KPI (id, definition, source tables, window, min n, exclusions, known biases): first_attempt_pass_rate = APPROVED_FINAL first attempts passing / first attempts, EXAM mode, rolling 4 weeks; eventual_pass_rate separately; criterion_performance = mean level/4 per criterion over APPROVED_FINAL attempts, n shown; probe_recall_7d / probe_recall_21d per LRN-19; transfer_pass_rate = passing TRANSFER observations / TRANSFER observations (LRN-25), n ≥10 before display; hint_dependence = T2+T3 hints per LAB hour and share of LAB observations with tier ≥2, stratified by declared difficulty; corrected_misconceptions = count RESOLVED (LRN-17); calibration per LRN-05; intervention_outcomes = MET / (MET+NOT_MET) with INCONCLUSIVE count shown; time_per_validated_competency = session minutes attributed via objective→competency mapping / competencies reaching VALIDATED, descriptive only and never an optimization target; review_backlog = due items not reviewed, bucketed by days overdue, plus block-capacity utilization. Every KPI query is a versioned, deterministic SQL/Rust function with a fixture oracle (R-014) and drilldown to observation ids.

location: v6.0 §18 'Scientific/learning effectiveness gates' B01-B06 (lines 541-549)
claim: B01 objective and rubric validity reviewed on unseen tasks; B02 retention/transfer not conflated with recall; B03 intervention measured against baseline; B04 effect size/uncertainty, inconclusive allowed; B05 correct a hypothesis and see plan revisions; B06 planning overhead proportionate.
defect: None of the six gates has a pass/fail criterion or a test procedure, so they cannot be executed, cannot be reported as PASS/FAIL/NOT RUN, and cannot block a release label (ADAPTIVE EVALUATED) as §18 intends.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 541-549 give one-line 'evidence required' phrases only.
correction: Replace with executable criteria in docs/evaluations/effectiveness-gates.md: B01 = (i) every rubric criterion maps to ≥1 objective and ≥1 NICE TKS id (content validity matrix complete, 0 orphans); (ii) deterministic checkers score 100% on known-answer fixtures; (iii) qualitative criteria re-graded blind ≥7 days later (or by a second reviewer) on ≥20 artifacts reach exact-level agreement ≥80% or weighted kappa ≥0.6; (iv) AI-advisory vs final agreement reported (no threshold). B02 = KPI sources separated per LRN-19 and the recall=100%/transfer=0% synthetic fixture renders distinct values. B03 = at least one preregistered design (B) or (A) experiment completed per LRN-21 with the baseline policy and comparability dimensions (difficulty, domain, assistance, program week) documented. B04 = every experiment report shows estimate, 95% interval, MID and classification; the synthetic oracle test passes. B05 = integration test: RETRACT a hypothesis → affected observations superseded → state replay differs as expected → a new schedule proposal is generated and the diff is displayed. B06 = (planning + approval + review UI minutes, from the session ledger, excluding curriculum evidence_reporting blocks) / study minutes ≤ 0.10 over a rolling 2-week window; measured, not estimated.

location: v6.0 C22 (line 88); §5 line 163 ('never assume introductory knowledge'); Section 23 CURRICULUM (line 970: 'Baseline competence calibration should allow accelerated study for already demonstrated skills'); §3 Audit C 'baseline diagnostic' (line 130)
claim: Start with a diagnostic calibration and optional accelerated pathways while preserving canonical content and opt-in skip decisions.
defect: The diagnostic has no design: what is sampled, at what difficulty, how a result maps to state and to skipping, what happens to the planned totals, and how diagnostic items interact with the exam bank (they are consumed). For an expert learner the early weekly practicals will sit at ceiling, so any 'learning lift' experiment on those clusters is unmeasurable; the document does not restrict experiments to below-ceiling clusters. Skipping guided blocks also removes the Recall/Understanding observations the state model expects.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 88, 130, 163, 970 contain no diagnostic specification. Ceiling-effect risk is INFERRED from the expert persona.
correction: Diagnostic design (Stage 04, DIAGNOSTIC mode, no hints): per competency cluster of each week-module, one sealed TRANSFER-level item at declared difficulty ≥ the cluster target plus a 5-item recall/understanding probe; items drawn from the bank and marked EXPOSED (bank sizing in LRN-13 adds +1 per cluster for the diagnostic). Mapping: pass (LRN-10 rule) → APPLICATION state INDEPENDENT (provisional) and TRANSFER observation recorded; skip eligibility = INDEPENDENT on all clusters of a day; a skip is an opt-in schedule_decisions row that converts guided_lab/independent_lab blocks of that day into validation/transfer work; planned minutes remain 420/300 in the base plan and actual minutes are recorded separately (no rewrite of planned totals). State rule for skipped clusters: VALIDATED still requires the EXAM and TRANSFER evidence of LRN-09; Recall/Understanding dimensions are marked NOT_REQUIRED_BY_PATHWAY rather than UNASSESSED. Experiments: method_experiments.eligible_clusters must exclude clusters whose diagnostic score ≥ 90% (ceiling); report diagnostic score distribution before any experiment.

location: v6.0 §9 line 273 ('Transfer: solve unfamiliar task/context'); §10 line 337 ('transfer generation with benchmarked novelty'); M08 row line 190; L03 row line 389
claim: Transfer = solve unfamiliar task/context; adaptive transfer generation with benchmarked novelty.
defect: 'Unfamiliar' and 'novelty' are not operationalized, so the same task could be counted as both an Application and a Transfer observation, and AI-generated 'transfer' tasks could be near-duplicates of exposed fixtures or carry public solutions. No rule separates near from far transfer or requires a validated key before a generated task yields evidence.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 190, 273, 337, 389 define no novelty criterion.
correction: Declare transfer dimensions per competency pack: tool, OS/platform, data format, protocol, role/context, scale, adversary technique variant. A task qualifies as TRANSFER for a learner iff its fixture family has zero exposure (exposure_ledger) and it differs from every exposed task for that competency on ≥1 declared dimension (near) or ≥2 (far); near/far is stored on the observation. An observation is APPLICATION when the family or a sibling variant was exposed in STUDY/LAB. Generated tasks: an AI-generated task is status DRAFT until a human-reviewed key/check and difficulty rationale exist (REVIEWED→SEALED); DRAFT tasks produce observations with reliability_class=AI_ADVISORY that cannot change state. Novelty check at generation: no fixture-family match and normalized token-overlap with any exposed item < 0.5 (threshold versioned).

location: v6.0 §9 line 273: observation includes '... reviewer, provenance, uncertainty and recency'; M06 row line 188
claim: Each observation includes ... uncertainty and recency.
defect: 'Uncertainty' has no representation; a free numeric uncertainty invites pseudo-precision, and recency has no decay/expiry rule, so derived states are not reproducible from a defined computation.
evidence: VERIFIED: line 273 names the field without a type or rule.
correction: Represent uncertainty as the enum reliability_class (LRN-06) with a versioned weight table (DETERMINISTIC_CHECK 1.0, EXTERNAL_REVIEW 1.0, SELF_ADJUDICATED 0.6, AI_ADVISORY 0.0 for state purposes, SELF_REPORT 0.0) plus an optional free-text caveat; recency via valid_until per observation (defaults: APPLICATION/TRANSFER 90 days, RECALL/UNDERSTANDING 45 days, configurable per competency). State rules count weighted, in-window observations only; the weight table and windows are part of competency_version so A05 replay is exact.

location: v6.0 §16 Assessment state machine (line 505): 'AVAILABLE → STARTED → SUBMITTED → EVIDENCE_REVIEW → GRADED_PROVISIONAL → APPROVED_FINAL; RETAKE_NEW_ATTEMPT; seal answers'
claim: Assessment lifecycle as listed, with answer sealing.
defect: Missing states and guards for measurement integrity: no time-limit expiry transition (the 120-min blind practical needs a hard timer from M04), no INVALIDATED state for a flawed test or integrity breach (LRN-16), no DISPUTED path for grading disputes named in §9, and no precondition that STARTED requires a SEALED, blind-eligible variant.
evidence: VERIFIED: line 505 lists no such states; §9 line 291 mentions 'grading disputes' without a state.
correction: Add: STARTED requires item.status=SEALED and blind-eligibility (LRN-13); EXPIRED is reached automatically when the M04 timer passes the version's time limit, auto-sealing captured evidence as SUBMITTED with attempts.time_limit_exceeded=true (gate failure per LRN-10); DISPUTED may be entered from GRADED_PROVISIONAL or APPROVED_FINAL by the learner or reviewer, resolved to a superseding grade_decisions row (original immutable); INVALIDATED may be entered from any post-STARTED state by an operator decision with reason (FLAWED_TEST, EXPOSURE_BREACH, ENVIRONMENT_FAILURE) and supersedes derived observations.

location: v6.0 §11 'Skill promotion gates' (line 425): 'positive activation ≥95%, false activation ≤2% on a meaningful stratified test suite'
claim: Promotion thresholds: positive activation ≥95%, false activation ≤2%.
defect: Thresholds are stated without a minimum suite size, so they are not measurable claims: 19/20 positives has a 95% Wilson interval of 0.764-0.991, and 0/20 false activations has an upper bound of 0.161, far above 2%. Even 0/100 has an upper bound of 0.037.
correction: Per skill: ≥50 positive cases per stratum and ≥150 negative/adversarial cases per stratum; report point estimate with Wilson 95% interval; promotion requires the positive-activation interval lower bound ≥0.90 and zero false activations in ≥150 negatives (which bounds the rate at about 2% with 95% confidence), or an observed false-activation interval upper bound ≤0.02. Fixture counts and seeds are recorded in skill_evals.

location: v6.0 §13 'Evaluation sets' (line 480): 'Ensure training/retrieval doesn't contain holdout answers'; §9 Exam integrity (line 291); C16 (line 82: one model performs several roles)
claim: Keep holdouts out of training and prompt/context retrieval; one local model can act as teacher and examiner under different contexts.
defect: The local model's pretraining is not controllable and plausibly contains public write-ups for widely used labs (OverTheWire, retired HTB machines, public CTFs named in v5.1 §14); an expert learner may also already know them. If the same model generates exam items, it can reproduce public tasks whose solutions the learner has seen, and if the teacher's retrieval index contains exam fixtures the examiner/teacher separation is only nominal. No leakage test is defined.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 82, 291, 480; v5.1 §14 lists public lab sources. Pretraining contamination is INFERRED and unverifiable for a given model.
correction: (1) Official blind items are in-house, parametrized fixtures with seeded variation (hostnames, credentials, log contents, vulnerable parameters) so no public key exists; public lab content may be used for STUDY/LAB only and is tagged PUBLIC_SOURCE in the exposure ledger. (2) Learner declares prior familiarity per fixture family before use; familiar families are not blind-eligible. (3) Sealed exam content carries content_classification=EXAM_SEALED and is excluded from every teacher/retrieval index by g9-policy; a Stage 07 leakage suite prompts the teacher with each sealed task and asserts no key material (n-gram overlap ≥ 8 tokens with the key) appears in outputs, with the actual decision and output captured (R-007). (4) Model-generated items follow LRN-25 review before sealing.

location: v6.0 §10 step 7-8 (lines 317-319: reserve approved capacity; separate unseen reassessment and delayed transfer test); §8 line 249 (Saturday remediation 60 min); §8 Adaptive calendar (line 258)
claim: Reserve approved calendar capacity for interventions; conduct unseen practical reassessment and delayed transfer tests; no hidden workload growth.
defect: The only curriculum slot for remediation and retests is the Saturday remediation block: 12 × 60 = 720 minutes for the entire program. At 30-60 minutes per retest or transfer check this bounds measurable interventions to roughly 12-24, which the document never states; without the bound, intervention proposals will silently exceed capacity or be deferred past their retest windows (yielding INCONCLUSIVE outcomes).
evidence: VERIFIED arithmetic: seed JSON saturday_blocks remediation=60 on 12 assessment days = 720 min. Per-retest duration is ASSUMED.
correction: M03/P01 must model remediation capacity explicitly (capacity ledger per week) and reject or re-propose interventions whose retest window cannot be scheduled; interventions.scheduling_status ∈ {RESERVED, DEFERRED, UNSCHEDULABLE}; the experiments protocol declares the capacity-bounded maximum number of interventions per program and the dashboard shows reserved vs available remediation minutes. Any proposal to add capacity (e.g., using part of independent_lab blocks) is a seed deviation requiring reconciliation.

location: v6.0 §18 B01 (line 544); §17 execution KPI 'prediction error' (line 519) exists only for business; M13 row (line 195)
claim: B01 requires rubric validity review on unseen tasks; the system tracks prediction error for business commitments.
defect: The competency model's own predictions are never tested against outcomes, although this is the one validity check that is feasible for N=1 and would give B01 empirical teeth: a state model that says VALIDATED should predict blind performance better than base rate.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 195, 519, 544 contain no predictive-validity measure for the learner model.
correction: Before each blind practical, M13 stores a system forecast per sampled item: P(pass) derived from the current competency state by a versioned deterministic mapping (e.g., VALIDATED 0.85, INDEPENDENT 0.70, GUIDED 0.45, INTRODUCED 0.25, UNASSESSED base rate), in calibration_observations with actor=SYSTEM and forecast_type=STATE_PREDICTION. After grading, compute Brier skill score vs base rate and AUC over all system forecasts (report after ≥40 resolved). A BSS ≤ 0 after ≥80 forecasts flags the state policy version for review. Report alongside learner calibration, clearly labeled as the model's calibration.

location: v6.0 §13 'Evaluation sets' (line 480): 'novice/expert calibration cases'; §10 line 331 'confidence calibration'; L06 row (line 392); M13 row (line 195)
claim: 'Calibration' is used for model evaluation cases (adapting explanations to novice/expert level), for the learner's confidence calibration, and for the baseline diagnostic 'calibration' (C22).
defect: Three different meanings share one term across modules that will be built by different engineers, inviting mis-implemented KPIs (e.g., a 'calibration' score that is a model-eval rubric).

Rename §13 cases to 'novice/expert level-adaptation cases' and C22 to 'diagnostic baseline'.

location: v6.0 §17 line 517 'time per validated competency'; §15 line 498 'visible model uncertainty'
claim: Track time per validated competency; show visible model uncertainty in the UI.
defect: 'Time per validated competency' is a Goodhart-prone efficiency metric (optimizing it rewards lowering validation standards or avoiding hard competencies). 'Model uncertainty' displayed from the model's self-reported confidence is not calibrated and may be read by the learner as evidence quality.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 498, 517. Goodhart risk is INFERRED.
correction: Mark time_per_validated_competency as descriptive-only in kpi-definitions.md, never a target, never fed to the teacher or scheduler as an objective. Replace 'model uncertainty' in the UI with the evidence reliability_class of the underlying observations and the count of supporting observations; model self-confidence, if shown, is labeled 'model self-report (uncalibrated)' and excluded from KPIs.

location: v6.0 §10 line 331: 'Do not randomly withhold necessary safety guidance or needed accommodations'; §5 line 165 (hints prevented in EXAM mode)
claim: Experiments must not withhold necessary safety guidance or accommodations.
defect: Correct principle, but the boundary between 'safety guidance' (never withheld) and 'instructional hints' (the experimental manipulation) is undefined, so an experiment arm could either leak the manipulation through 'safety' messages or block genuinely needed lab-safety warnings. v5.1's 'fixed hints' control also never defined what the control arm receives.
evidence: VERIFIED: lines 165, 331; v5.1 line 34.
correction: Define a SAFETY message class in T05/T06 (scope boundaries, destructive-action warnings, authorization reminders, lab-isolation checks) delivered identically in every arm and mode (including EXAM) and logged with assistance_tier=0; instructional hints (T1-T3) are the only manipulable class. The control arm of any hint experiment is specified as 'fixed-tier policy: T1 on request, T2 after two failed attempts, never T3', stored in the preregistration record.

location: v6.0 §9 'Official assessment rubric' (lines 277-285) applied to all weekly assessments; Appendix A evidence artifacts (e.g., D07-D11 diagrams/maps, D49 'LLM threat model', D61 'AI threat model')
claim: One configurable baseline rubric (independent execution, root cause, remediation/verification, detection/visibility, evidence, scope) applies to assessments.

evidence: VERIFIED: rubric lines 277-285; Appendix A artifacts at lines 713-717 (network maps), 785 (LLM threat model), 809 (AI threat model), 813 (evaluation protocol).
